title: Direct sowing on a permanent bed
summary: Learn how to mark out rows and hand-sow small and large seeds at the right spacing and depth on a permanent bed.

pages.title: Successful direct sowing on a permanent bed
pages.illustration_description: Vue d'une planche de culture permanente en pleine terre bien nivelée (sans aucun bois ni coffrage), avec des sillons droits tracés parallèlement et des mains ouest-africaines semant délicatement des graines.

pages.title: Which plants should be direct-sown?
pages.text:
Direct sowing is done in **4 steps**. For one growing bed (**10 m × 75 cm**), one person can do the job by hand in less than two hours.

This technique is used for plants that are difficult to transplant, such as:
- Carrots, beets, radishes, turnips
- Green beans, peanuts, okra, cucumbers
- Green manures such as millet

Make sure your beds have already been **loosened, leveled, moistened and labeled**.
pages.illustration_description: Planche botanique en aquarelle regroupant des légumes adaptés au semis direct : carotte avec fanes, gousses de haricot vert, gombo, concombre et arachides disposés harmonieusement sur papier crème.

pages.title: Required equipment
pages.text:
Before you start, gather the following equipment:

- **Seeds** (check the expiry dates and quality)
- 1 straight stick or a 2-meter metal pipe
- 1 measuring tape and 1 distance marker
- 1 fine-toothed rake
- 1 watering can (if there is no sprinkler system)
- 1 label (sowing date and variety)
- Straw or dead leaves
- *Optional*: a protective net or insect mesh
pages.illustration_description: Outils de semis direct disposés en aquarelle botanique : sachets de graines sans texte, bâton droit, mètre ruban, râteau fin, traceur de distance, arrosoir et botte de paille sur la terre chaude.

pages.title: Step 1: Mark out the parallel rows
pages.text:
Start by determining the **sowing density**:
- The number of rows (examples: 1 row, 2 rows spaced 60 cm apart, 3 rows spaced 25 cm apart, 4 rows spaced 20 cm apart)
- The spacing between rows

You will find this information on the crop's technical sheet or on the seed packet.

Mark out the right number of rows with a marker or a stick. The rows must be **perfectly parallel** to make weeding and hilling easier.
pages.illustration_description: Un agriculteur ouest-africain debout dans le passe-pied en terre, tirant un traceur le long d'une planche de pleine terre nivelée pour dessiner trois rangs droits et parfaitement parallèles.

pages.title: Step 2: Sowing "small seeds" (1/2)
pages.text:
For small seeds such as **carrots, beets, radishes and turnips**:

1. Make a **furrow 1 cm deep** by pressing a straight stick along the marked rows, from the start to the end of the bed.
2. Place the seeds in the furrow, following the recommended spacing.
pages.illustration_description: Gros plan en aquarelle sur des mains ouest-africaines appuyant un bâton droit dans la terre fine pour former un sillon peu profond, puis déposant délicatement de fines graines le long du sillon.

pages.title: Step 2: Sowing "small seeds" (2/2)
pages.text:
3. With the same stick, **lightly press the seeds** into the bottom of the furrow to remove air pockets. This ensures good contact between the seeds and the soil and prevents them from rotting.
4. **Close the furrow** with fine soil and, if needed, firm it lightly with the back of your hand.
pages.illustration_description: Coupe transversale pédagogique en aquarelle montrant de petites graines bien plaquées au fond d'un sillon peu profond recouvert de terre fine, avec une main ouest-africaine tassant doucement la surface.

pages.title: Step 3: Sowing "large seeds" — The grid pattern
pages.text:
For large seeds such as **beans, peanuts, okra, squash, zucchini and cucumbers**:

1. The lines corresponding to the rows were already marked in step 1.
2. Now mark out a **grid** with a stick or a marker, spacing the perpendicular lines according to the distance between seeds given on the technical sheet.
3. The **grid intersections** show you exactly where to place the seeds.
pages.illustration_description: Vue de dessus en biais d'une planche de culture en pleine terre où un quadrillage régulier est tracé dans la terre fine, montrant clairement les intersections prêtes à recevoir les grosses graines.

pages.title: Step 3: Pushing in and covering large seeds
pages.text:
4. Place one seed at each grid intersection. Push it in with your thumb to a depth of **2 to 3 times the size of the seed** (or as indicated on the packet).
5. Cover the seeds with soil and firm lightly to ensure good contact with the soil.
pages.illustration_description: Gros plan en aquarelle d'un pouce ouest-africain enfonçant une graine de haricot à l'intersection d'un quadrillage tracé sur une planche de pleine terre, avec une coupe montrant la profondeur adaptée.

pages.title: Step 4: What to do after sowing?
pages.text:
After sowing, several essential tasks remain to ensure good seedling emergence:

- A gentle, even **initial watering**
- A **thin layer of mulch** to protect the surface
- Later: **hoeing**, **hilling** and **weeding**

See module **M3.4.4** to learn this post-sowing care in detail.
pages.illustration_description: Une agricultrice ouest-africaine arrosant en pluie très fine avec un arrosoir une planche de pleine terre fraîchement semée et recouverte d'un léger voile de paille.

pages.title: Congratulations! Your direct sowing is complete
pages.text:
**Congratulations**, you have just completed your first direct-sown bed, using the right spacing and depths!

You can repeat this operation on all the other beds planned for direct sowing.
pages.illustration_description: Planche permanente en pleine terre paillée montrant de jeunes plantules vertes levant en rangs parfaitement alignés et réguliers sous la lumière douce du matin en Afrique de l'Ouest.
